message: The invoice currency code (BT-5) at {@/BT-5} is {/BT-5}, which is not on the iso-4217 snapshot this pack decides against.
note: The identifier of this rule is the official validation artefacts' and not the standard's: clause 6.3 names the code list of each business term in the semantic model table and gives the restriction no rule identifier of its own. The identifier is kept so that a report can be compared with theirs. The snapshot is ISO's own list of the day it was taken and the artefacts carry a 178-code listing of their own, so the two differ in both directions: measured on 2026-09-20, the artefacts accept CNH and STD which the snapshot does not carry, and the snapshot accepts STN and XAD which the artefacts do not. An invoice in one of those four codes is therefore judged differently by the two engines. The code list directory records which day was taken and why, and the conformance ledger carries the divergence.

note: The identifier of this rule is the official validation artefacts' and not the standard's: clause 6.3 names the code list of each business term in the semantic model table and gives the restriction no rule identifier of its own. The identifier is kept so that a report can be compared with theirs. The artefacts split the VAT category codes over two identifiers, and they split them by the element the syntax writes rather than by the business term: this one is the category of a document level allowance and of a document level charge, which both syntaxes decide under this identifier.

message: A VAT category code of a VAT breakdown (BT-118) or of an invoiced item (BT-151) is not on the untdid-5305 snapshot this pack decides against; the paths of this finding name where.
note: The identifier of this rule is the official validation artefacts' and not the standard's: clause 6.3 names the code list of each business term in the semantic model table and gives the restriction no rule identifier of its own. The identifier is kept so that a report can be compared with theirs. The category of an invoiced item is decided under this identifier by both syntaxes. The category of a VAT breakdown is not: the CII artefact decides it here and the UBL artefact decides it as BR-CL-17, because each numbers the rule after the element its syntax writes. A rule of this engine is a statement about a business term and cannot follow both, so it follows the CII reading and conformance/rules/ledger.md records the consequence for a report compared with the UBL artefact.
